newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Keppel-financed power plant opens in Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: Keppel-financed power plant opens in Nicaragua.

text.p: Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman on Monday inaugurated a $50 million power plant financed primarily by a unit of Singapore's Keppel Corporation, the government said.

The 30-megawatt plant, built in less than a year at Puerto Sandino on Nicaragua's Pacific Coast, will provide this Central American country with between 10 percent and 18 percent of its power capacity, the government said in a news release.
The project was financed by Amfels Inc., a subsidiary of Keppel Fels, in conjunction with CENSA, a Nicaraguan corporation set up for the construction of the plant.
During the inauguration ceremony, Aleman announced that his government soon would open bidding on construction of a 50-megawatt plant to be followed by a 150-megawatt plant in 2000.

"The country and the people demand services that we are obligated to provide in the short and long term," said Aleman, who two weeks ago fired his Energy Minister after severe energy shortages caused long blackouts in the capital city Managua.
Shun Chan Ben, executive director of the Keppel Corporation, said this was the company's first investment in Central America.
"This investment will open the eyes of other investors," Shun Chan Ben said, according to the press release.
